decision.explanation: The question asks 'When was the Croatian money introduced?' and the provided sources distinguish two distinct introductions of the Croatian kuna. The first introduction occurred on 26 July 1941 under the Independent State of Croatia during World War II (supported by D2S5, D3S2, D4S1). The second introduction refers to the modern kuna, which was introduced on May 30, 1994, marking a transition from the Croatian dinar (supported by D1S3). Both dates refer to the same currency name ('kuna') but different historical contexts and are thus valid and distinct answers.
